newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-TRAIL BLAZERS NAME MIKE DUNLEAVY COACH.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-TRAIL BLAZERS NAME MIKE DUNLEAVY COACH.

text.p: Mike Dunleavy, who last month stepped down as general manager of the Milwaukee Bucks, on Tuesday was named new head coach of the Portland Trail Blazers.
Dunleavy, who had previously coached the Bucks and Los Angeles Lakers, succeeds P.J. Carlesimo, who was fired last week after three years as Portland coach.

"I'm excited about joining the Trail Blazer organisation," Dunleavy said. "I can't wait to get started as we all strive to give the great fans of Portland what they deserve -- another world championship."

Portland's only NBA title came in 1977. The Trail Blazers have made the playoffs 15 consecutive seasons -- the longest current streak in the NBA -- but have been eliminated in the first round the past five years.
Dunleavy took the Lakers to the NBA Finals in 1991 before falling to the Chicago Bulls, but failed to make the playoffs in four seasons as Milwaukee coach.

The 43-year-old Dunleavy inherits a young team long on talent but short on discipline. The lineup includes guards Kenny Anderson and Isaiah Rider and forwards Rasheed Wallace and Gary Trent. All but Anderson have had off-court problems and each starter was benched at least once this season for team rules violations.

"I'm confident that teaming Mike with our core group of young, athletic players gives the Blazers a strong foundation on which to build our future," said Portland president Bob Whitsitt at a news conference to announce Dunleavy's hiring.
In four seasons as Bucks coach, Dunleavy compiled a 107-221 mark, before stepping down in April 1996 while retaining his front office duties. He was 101-63 with the Lakers.
The Blazers finished 49-33 mark this season but were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs by the Lakers, marking their third straight first-round exit under Carlesimo.
